title: Cardiopulmonary Assessment and Exercise Monitoring

book.title: Cardiopulmonary Assessment and Exercise Monitoring
book.lead: Every cardiopulmonary chapter depends on this one. Learn to read the patient before you move the patient.

blocks.text: In cardiopulmonary physiotherapy, the main safety question is not "Which tissue hurts?" but "Can this patient's heart and lungs tolerate what I am about to ask?" A structured assessment answers that question and gives you the numbers to monitor during treatment.

sections.title: 10.2 Chart review before you see the patient

rows: Trends in heart rate (HR), blood pressure (BP), respiratory rate (RR), SpO2, temperature
For example 94 to 98% for most, 88 to 92% for patients at risk of hypercapnia [Ref – to verify BTS guideline]
Haemoglobin, white cells, CRP, potassium, troponin
Beta-blockers (blunt HR response), bronchodilators, anticoagulants, inotropes
Around 120/80 mmHg; treatment thresholds per local guidance
About 94 to 98% on room air (lower in some chronic lung disease)
10 to 13 kPa (75 to 100 mmHg) on room air

blocks.text: Reading a blood gas in four steps

items: **pH**: below 7.35 acidaemia; above 7.45 alkalaemia.
**PaCO2** (respiratory part): high CO2 makes the blood acidic.
**HCO3** (metabolic part): low bicarbonate makes the blood acidic.
**Which one explains the pH?** That is the primary problem. Is the other one moving to compensate?

blocks.label: CLINICAL CASE
body: pH 7.29, PaCO2 8.2 kPa, HCO3 30. pH is low (acidaemia); CO2 is high, which explains the acid: **respiratory** **acidosis**. HCO3 is raised, showing partial metabolic compensation, suggesting the CO2 rise has been present for some time (acute-on-chronic). In a COPD patient this signals hypercapnic respiratory failure; avoid excessive oxygen and inform the team.

rows: When? At rest or on exertion? How far can you walk? (Use mMRC dyspnoea scale)
Productive? How much sputum, what colour, any blood?
Stairs, self-care, work, sleep position (number of pillows for orthopnoea)
Smoking (pack-years = packs per day × years), occupation, previous admissions, home oxygen

items: **General observation**: posture, use of accessory muscles, pursed-lip breathing, ability to speak in full sentences, cyanosis, finger clubbing, ankle swelling.
**Breathing pattern**: rate, depth, ratio of inspiration to expiration, chest wall symmetry, paradoxical movement.
**Palpation**: chest expansion, tracheal position.
**Percussion**: dull (consolidation, effusion) versus hyper-resonant (pneumothorax, hyperinflation).
**Auscultation**: compare left and right at the same level, front, side and back.

rows: Harsh, expiration as long as inspiration, heard at the periphery

items: 30-metre flat corridor with cones at each end.
Patient rests for 10 minutes; record HR, BP, SpO2, Borg dyspnoea and fatigue.
Instruction: "Walk as far as possible for 6 minutes. You may slow down and rest if needed."
Use standard phrases of encouragement at each minute only [Ref – to verify ATS/ERS standard].
Record distance, lowest SpO2, highest HR, Borg scores, and rests.

blocks.text: Other tests: Incremental and Endurance Shuttle Walk Tests, 1-minute sit-to-stand, cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) in specialist settings.

rows: About 11 to 14 ("fairly light" to "somewhat hard") for moderate training [Ref – to verify]
About 3 to 4 ("moderate" to "somewhat severe") in pulmonary rehabilitation [Ref – to verify]

items: **Karvonen (heart rate reserve) method**: target HR = ((HRmax − HRrest) × intensity %) + HRrest. Example: age-predicted HRmax 220 − 60 = 160; HRrest 70; intensity 50%: ((160 − 70) × 0.5) + 70 = 115 beats per minute.
In patients on beta-blockers, HR response is blunted: use RPE instead.

sections.title: 10.7 When not to start and when to stop exercise

rows: Unstable angina, chest pain at rest
Resting HR above about 120 or new uncontrolled arrhythmia
Resting systolic BP above about 180 or diastolic above about 110 mmHg
Systolic BP falling with increasing workload, or excessive rise (for example above about 250/115)
Resting SpO2 below the patient's prescribed target despite oxygen
SpO2 dropping below target and not recovering quickly
Severe breathlessness, dizziness, confusion, pallor, cyanosis, ataxia
Recent acute myocardial infarction without clearance

blocks.text: Thresholds are commonly quoted guidance; confirm with local protocol and ACSM-style criteria [Ref – to verify].

blocks.label: TEACHER'S VOICE
body: Always take baseline vital signs, monitor during, and record recovery afterwards. Recovery speed is information: a patient whose HR and SpO2 return to baseline within 2 to 3 minutes is tolerating the load well.

items: **pH 7.48, PaCO2 3.6 kPa, HCO3 24. Interpret.** Respiratory alkalosis (often from hyperventilation, pain or anxiety), uncompensated.
**Why use RPE in patients on beta-blockers?** HR does not rise normally with effort.
**Calculate a 60% HRR target for HRmax 170, HRrest 70.** ((170 − 70) × 0.6) + 70 = 130 beats per minute.
**Bronchial breathing at the right base suggests?** Consolidation.
**During exercise, systolic BP falls as the workload rises. Action?** Stop; this is an abnormal response requiring medical review.

sections.title: Now You Should Be Able To

items: Perform a structured cardiopulmonary assessment and interpret a blood gas.
Auscultate and interpret breath sounds.
Conduct a 6MWT and set exercise intensity using HRR and Borg.
Apply start and stop criteria safely.

sections.10-1-why-this-chapter-comes-first: Dil aur phephron ki physio mein sab se ahem sawaal yeh hai ke kya patient exercise ke liye mehfooz hai. Yeh chapter is ka tareeqa sikhata hai.
sections.10-2-chart-review-before-you-see-the-pat: Patient ko dekhne se pehle chart parhein: diagnosis, oxygen, vital signs ka rujhan, lab results aur doctor ki pabandiyan.
sections.10-3-normal-adult-values-resting-typical: Normal adult values: dhadkan 60-100, saans 12-20, SpO2 aam taur par 94-98%, aur BP. In se muqabla kar ke faisla karein.
sections.10-4-subjective-assessment: Saans phoolna kab aur kitna, khansi aur balgham, seene ka dard aur roz ke kaam ki salahiyat poochein.
sections.10-5-objective-assessment: Dekhna (posture, gardan ki muscles se saans), seene ki aawaz, seene ka phailao, sujan aur vital signs.
sections.10-6-exercise-testing: 6-minute walk test 30 metre ki seedhi raahdari mein: faasla, SpO2, dhadkan aur saans ki takleef note karein.
sections.10-7-when-not-to-start-and-when-to-stop-: Kab exercise shuru na karein aur kab rokein: aaraam mein seene ka dard, SpO2 ka bohat girna, BP ya dhadkan ka ghair-mehfooz hona.
sections.10-8-questions-with-answers: Sawaal hal karein, khaas kar blood gas parhne ki practice.
sections.now-you-should-be-able-to: Yeh checklist hai. Har point khud kar sakein to tick karein.
